title: The Upsweep Ocean Sound Mystery
hook: What is the source of the mysterious Upsweep sound?
headline: Ocean's Deep Rumble Still Unexplained

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In August 1991, NOAA hydrophones near Hawaii recorded a low-frequency hum using the equatorial autonomous hydrophone arrays.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Scientists noted the Upsweep consists of vertical sweeps lasting about three seconds each, not a three-day rise from 20 to 30 hertz.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Similar low-frequency rumbles were later detected near the Azores in 1993.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: One theory links the Upsweep to a distant iceberg fracture, though no ice nearby.

end.line: What could be creating this oceanic mystery?

description: Explore the puzzling Upsweep ocean sound and the clues that keep scientists guessing.

facts.claim: In May 1991 NOAA hydrophones near Hawaii recorded a low-frequency hum
The sound's frequency rose from about 20 Hz to 30 Hz over three days
A similar low-frequency signal was detected near the Azores in 1993
One hypothesis links the Upsweep to a distant iceberg fracture, but no ice exists in the recording area
